items.title: In Jharkhand, even jails are not safe: Babulal Marandi
points: The Leader of the Opposition in the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly Babulal Marandi cited the incidents of including the sexual assault of a youth in Hotwar Jail, the alleged rape of a minor girl by a Congress MLA from Simdega, and the alleged rape of a…

File. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The Leader of the Opposition in the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly Babulal Marandi on Saturday (November 14, 2026), cornered the State Government over a series of criminal incidents.

He cited the incidents of including the sexual assault of a youth in Hotwar Jail, the alleged rape of a minor girl by a Congress MLA from Simdega, and the alleged rape of a woman who had gone to the Gamharia police station seeking justice.

Fifteen police officers were suspended in connection with the alleged rape of a 20-year-old woman on the premises of the Gamharia police station in Jharkhand, Saraikela-Kharsawan district, on November 1, 2026.

items.title: Mumbai police announce traffic diversion ahead of Britain’s Prince William visit
points: This image is used for representational purposes only. | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto Mumbai Police on Saturday (November 14, 2026) have announced traffic diversions, road closures and parking restrictions across parts of south Mumbai from…
The restrictions come ahead of Britain’s Prince William’s visit to Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize awards ceremony.
The ceremony is hosted in Mumbai from November 16 to 18 for the sixth annual Earthshot Prize.

The notification issued by Hemrajsingh Rajput, Deputy Commissioner of Police (South), Traffic, Mumbai, includes changes to traffic movement around Hutatma Rajguru Chowk, Shaheed Bhagatsingh Marg, Ballard Pier and several roads in the NCPA area.
Shah Marg road and Dorabji Tata Road for 24 hours, and on November 16, the parking is suspended from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Moraji Road, J.

The U-turn from Free Press Road’s northbound carriageway at Hutatma Rajguru Chowk towards the southbound carriageway will be permitted during this period and the right turn from Madam Cama Road towards Free press road will remain open.

items.title: 4.5 magnitude earthquake tremors felt in Maharashtra’s Jalgaon
points: Image used for representational purposes only. | Photo Credit: Reuters Maharashtra’s Jalgaon district felt earthquake tremors of 4.6 magnitude on Saturday (November 14, 2026), raising concerns among the citizens, the district officials said on Tuesday.
The tremors were felt at around 9.16 a.m. in the Satpuda region, including Yawal, Raver, Chopda and Bhusawal taluka, with its epicentre located in Madhya Pradesh’s Khargone district.
District Collector Rohan Ghuge said, “No loss of life or property damage in Jalgaon has been reported.
Residents should not panic or fall prey to any rumours.” Jalgaon also houses three major dams, including Hatnur, Waghur and Girna.
One of the concerns was potential seismic risks in these regions due to the tremors.
However, nothing happened, cleared the Jalgaon District officials, Earlier in August, Maharashtra’s Palghar felt two back-to-back tremors of magnitude 3.4 in a span of an hour.

items.title: Man held for conducting ‘reconnaissance’ of sensitive locations in Mumbai
points: Yash Singh, a resident of Airoli in Navi Mumbai, was initially detained by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) based on inputs regarding his social media contacts with anti-national handlers.
He was subsequently taken into custody by the Keralam police in connection with a case registered in the Thrissur district in the southern state, the official said.
Singh told the police that he was tasked by social media handlers linked to mafia gangs and subversive elements to carry out a recce of sensitive areas of South Mumbai, particularly around Colaba.
“His assignments included photographing and pinpointing the exact locations of the Chabad House, businesses owned by Jewish individuals, and areas frequented by foreign nationals.
Chabad House was among the locations targeted by Pakistani terrorists during the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks in 2008.

Further investigation established that Singh was allegedly in direct contact with anti-national elements through the messaging platform Telegram, linking him to an accused already arrested in a case registered at the Thrissur East police station in Keralam…

items.title: TGPCB recommends closures, forfeitures over dusty construction
points: The Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) has received several complaints regarding air pollution caused by dust emissions from construction projects in the Tellapur and Kollur areas of Sangareddy district.

After receiving several complaints of air pollution due to construction, the Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) constituted Rolling Task Force Teams to these projects and assess compliance with environmental regulations and implementation of air pollution…
The team embarked on inspections and observed dust emissions from construction activity was aggravating air pollution.
The Committee reviewed the environmental compliance of as many as 16 construction projects.
A period of 10 days was recommended for the concerned projects to rectify the violations.
Three construction projects began construction activity without obtaining Consent for Establishment (CFE) from the Pollution Control Board, the TGPCB stated.

Two others were continuing construction activities in violation of the Orders for Suspension of Operations previously issued by the TGPCB, without obtaining permission from the Board for revocation of the suspension orders.

items.title: Six-month traffic disruption ahead as Ranigunj railway underpass work to begin in Hyderabad
points: Work on widening the Ranigunj Road Under Bridge (RuB) is expected to begin within a week.
The existing carriageway, which is around 13 metres wide and currently accommodates two-way traffic, will be expanded to 22 metres to facilitate four-way movement.

Under the proposed plan, vehicles travelling from MG Road towards Paradise and Ranigunj will be asked to take a left towards Distillery Road, pass through another road underbridge and proceed towards Karbala before joining MG Road.
Officials said that if congestion builds up near Karbala Maidan, a portion of the traffic will be diverted through Minister Road and Rasoolpura.

Hyderabad, Telangana, 14/11/2026: A view of Ranigunj railway underpass near James Street railway station as part of the six-month traffic disruption ahead as underpass work to begin, in Secunderabad on Saturday, November 14, 2026.
Chandra Shekar, who works at the Nampally court, commutes every day from Bolarum to reach work by 9 a.m., travelling through the stretch during the morning rush hour.

points: Traffic restrictions and diversions will be implemented on stretches between Srinagar Colony T-Junction and NTR Bhavan on Road No. 2, Banjara Hills, in view of the ongoing construction of a steel flyover between Jubilee Hills Check Post and NFCL under the…

According to the traffic advisory issued on Saturday, vehicles travelling from Srinagar Colony towards SNT Junction near the TV9 office and Road No. 2, Banjara Hills, will not be allowed to take a right turn at SNT Junction.
Commuters will have to take a left turn and make a U-turn at NFCL to reach Road No. 2.

Vehicles coming from Begumpet towards SNT, Sagar Society, KBR Park entrance, Jubilee Hills Check Post, Road Nos. 36 and 45, and the Durgam Cheruvu Cable Bridge will have to take the Panjagutta Flyover ‘Y’ Junction towards Taj Krishna and Road No. 1,…
They should then take a right turn at the 1/10 Banjara Hills Junction towards Zaheranagar, Basavatarakam Cancer Hospital and Agarasen Island to reach their destinations.

items.title: Telangana Greyhounds get new shooting range at Rajendranagar
points: DGP CV Anand with Anil Kumar, Director General of Police (Operations) and head of the Greyhounds and OCTOPUS units, and other senior officers at the Telangana Greyhounds facility in Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, on Saturday.

Anand on Saturday inaugurated the SPS OODA Shoot House at the Telangana Greyhounds facility in Rajendranagar, with the unit asked to maintain its strength at no less than 700 personnel, and continue rigorous operational training.
The OODA concept, which stands for Observe, Orient, Decide and Act, has been incorporated into its training approach to help commandos assess situations, make decisions and respond quickly.

Speaking at the event, Mr. Anand described the Telangana Greyhounds as a model for police forces across the country and said the unit, along with OCTOPUS, played an important role in addressing threats such as Naxalism, terrorism and hijackings.
He recalled the role played by the Greyhounds in tackling Naxalite activities and terrorist threats during the 1980s.

items.title: Eight varieties of pharmaceutical ingredients worth ₹3.54 lakh seized in TG SAFE raid at Ameenpur firm
points: The raid was conducted at Neocell Biotechnologies Private Limited, located at the Medical Devices Park in Sultanpur, on Friday, following credible information about the illegal stocking of pharmaceutical ingredients for sale without a valid drug licence.
According to TG SAFE, officials found eight varieties of APIs illegally stocked at the premises and seized drug stocks worth ₹3.54 lakh.
Further investigation is under way, and action will be initiated against those responsible in accordance with the law, TG SAFE said.
They further added that stocking APIs for sale without a valid drug licence is punishable under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, with imprisonment of up to five years.
TG SAFE’s Drugs Wing is responsible for issuing licences for the stocking and sale of APIs under the Act.

items.title: Four arrested for illegal sand extraction in Madgul
points: Four persons were arrested for allegedly extracting sand illegally from Madgul lake and transporting it without authorisation during the early hours of November 11.
The accused were identified as Kasani Mallesh, Gaddam Jangaiah, M.
According to Madgul police, they excavated soil from the lake, filtered it to extract sand and transported it illegally at around 3 a.m.
Police arrested the four as part of the investigation and produced them before a magistrate at Amangal.
The court remanded them to judicial custody for 15 days, following which they were shifted to Chanchalguda Central Prison.
The Future City police warned that strict legal action would be taken against those involved in illegal sand extraction, transportation and other unlawful activities.

items.title: 25 kg of chloral hydrate seized, five arrested in adulterated toddy raids
points: Five people were arrested and 25 kg of chloral hydrate was seized during three separate operations by the Malkajgiri Excise Department against the adulteration of toddy and the illegal supply of the prohibited chemical.
A total of 264 litres of adulterated toddy was also destroyed.
On Friday, the District Task Force (DTF), along with the Malkajgiri Station House Officer, raided a toddy centre in East Anandbagh and found that chloral hydrate had been mixed with the toddy.
Officials collected samples in the presence of witnesses and destroyed 163 litres of adulterated toddy.
In a separate operation, the DTF team, along with the Nacharam SHO, inspected a toddy centre in Ashok Nagar and detected the use of chloral hydrate.
Officials destroyed 101 litres of adulterated toddy after collecting samples.
As part of the investigation to trace the source of the chemical, the Excise Department arrested its alleged supplier, Siddagoni Rangaiah, at Pilaipalli village in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district.
Around 25 kg of chloral hydrate was seized from his possession.

items.title: 4,252 motorists booked for using mobile phones while driving
points: Hyderabad traffic police booked 4,252 motorists who were caught using mobile phones while driving during a special enforcement drive conducted between November 8 and November 14.
Of those booked, 3,548 were two-wheeler riders, 42 - three-wheeler drivers, and 662 - four-wheeler drivers, according to a press note issued on Saturday.
The drive was conducted as part of efforts to improve road safety, promote disciplined driving and prevent accidents caused by distracted driving.

The traffic police said using a mobile phone while driving causes cognitive, visual and manual distraction, affecting a driver’s attention, reaction time and judgement, and increasing the risk of collisions.
The police said they were following a zero-tolerance policy towards mobile phone use while driving and would continue to conduct special enforcement drives regularly.

items.title: Synod of Jacobite Church approves steps to canonise Patriarch Ignatius Peter III
points: The Episcopal Synod of the Jacobite Syrian Church on Saturday (November 14) decided to complete the procedures to canonise Patriarch Ignatius Peter III, who convened the historic Mulanthuruthy Synod in 1876.
The decision was taken as Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II, the supreme head of the Universal Syrian Orthodox Church, accepted the Jacobite Church’s request to declare Ignatius Peter III a saint.

A statement by the Jacobite Syrian Church said the decision was taken at a meeting of the Episcopal Synod, chaired by Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II, at the Marthoman Cathedral in Mulanthuruthy during the 150th anniversary celebrations of the Mulanthuruthy…
Addressing the synod, the Patriarch called for collective efforts to establish lasting peace in the Malankara Church.
Hailing from Mosul, Ignatius Peter III was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1872 until he died in 1894.

items.title: Police intensify investigation in sexual harassment case against TVK functionary
points: The Coimbatore District Police have intensified investigation into the allegations by a woman functionary of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) that Karamadai union secretary of the party sexually harassed her in May this year.
Coimbatore District Superintendent of Police A.
Pavan Kumar Reddy said the investigating officer would also verify some of the audio tapes and videos, which the complainant had claimed as evidence to back her allegations.
TVK’s Karamadai union secretary Karupusamy, party worker Sabitha, and her husband Pandi are the three accused in the case.

The complainant, aged 29, who formerly held the post of the party’s secretary at a panchayat in Karamadai union, has alleged that she was removed from her post after she questioned Karupusamy over the alleged sexual harassment.

Panneerselvam of Samooga Neethi Katchi, who has been offering legal assistance to the complainant, alleged that the police were not keen on arresting the accused despite having registered a case against them for serious offences.
Sunil Anand before the case was registered has surfaced.

items.title: BJP to stage protest against TVK’s Kallakurichi MLA on Nov. 18
points: The BJP will hold a demonstration in Kallakurichi on November 18 against TVK’s Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh, who had allegedly sent inappropriate messages to the district Collector.
State BJP president Nainar Nagenthran told journalists in Chennai on Saturday that the protest will be led by former Telangana Governor Tamilisai Soundararajan.

Addressing reporters at Kamalalayam, the party headquarters, Mr. Nagenthran alleged the State government had failed to act on complaints relating to the case and demanded accountability from the ruling government.
Referring to reports of missing children, including seven girls among 12 persons reported missing in Cuddalore district, he questioned the government’s response to concerns over women’s safety.
Citing a proposed investment of ₹15,000 crore by a Hyundai group company in Andhra Pradesh, he said the government should address the concerns of industries.
He also claimed the State’s GST revenue growth had declined from 5% to minus 5% and attributed this to manufacturing units moving to neighbouring States.
He urged the Chief Minister to take immediate steps to address the situation.

items.title: Take necessary steps to control inflation, Dhinakaran tells T.N. govt.
points: Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V.
Dhinakaran on Saturday said Tamil Nadu ranks first in India in price rise and urged the TVK-led government to take necessary measures to control the surge in prices of essential commodities.

Stating Tamil Nadu holds the top spot in India for price hikes as retail inflation in the State has risen to 7.29 per cent, Mr. Dhinakaran said this occurred as a result of negligence in monitoring the price rise and failing to take timely action to…
Mr. Dhinakaran said Tamil Nadu, which was once a pioneering state in India, has been pushed into an abyss over the past six months due to the inefficient administration of the TVK rule.

He demanded that the government abandon efforts to divert the public through false propaganda on social media via “Paid Virtual Warriors,” and immediately undertake constructive measures necessary to control the price rise of essential commodities.

items.title: Investment promotion panel holds first meeting, targets $72 billion in exports
points: The first meeting of the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission (TNIPC) was held under the chairmanship of Chief Secretary Sai Kumar, with discussions focusing on the proposed new industrial policy, single-window clearances, progress of investment…
During the meeting, the preparatory work for the New Industrial Policy 2027 was reviewed.
Since May 2026, the government has signed 112 MoUs, representing proposed investments exceeding ₹1.14 lakh crore and the potential to generate employment for 1,32,771 persons.
The State aims to increase its exports from the present $59 billion to $72 billion.
With all these initiatives, Tamil Nadu intends to become a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036.

The Commission was constituted on November 3, 2026, under Section 16 A of the Tamil Nadu Business Facilitation Act, 2018, as amended through the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion and Facilitation Legislation, 2026.

It comprises 20 members representing various key government departments, including Finance, Energy, Information Technology, Housing and Urban Development, Transport, Environment, Labour Welfare and Commercial Taxes, among others.

items.title: Youth, two juveniles held for ATM robbery attempt in Vellore
points: Prasanth, and two juveniles were arrested by Gudiyatham Town police on Saturday for allegedly damaging an ATM of a public sector bank in an attempt to steal cash.
The suspects were residents of Perumbadi village near Tirupattur town.
A special police patrol team had noticed three persons running out from the ATM kiosk on October 31.
The team rushed to the kiosk and found the machine to be damaged.
Lubricants were sprayed on the CCTV cameras inside the kiosk.
The team also seized sharp weapons that could have been used to break open the machine.

points: A gang of four persons were arrested by Tirupattur Taluk police on Saturday for robbery in the area.
The arrested persons were identified as S.
Ritish, 22, all residents of Tirupattur.
Damodharan, 29, was running a two-wheeler mechanic shop in Tirupattur town.
He was returning home when the gang intercepted him and demanded cash and valuables.
When he resisted, the ganga allegedly attacked and robbed him of ₹10,000 cash and a mobile phone and fled the scene.
The police said that an injured Damodharan reached Government Taluk Hospital in Tirupattur town for treatment.
On being informed by hospital authorities, Tirupattur Taluk police conducted an inquiry with Damodharan.

items.title: AIADMK to protest seeking action against Deputy Speaker in Thuraiyur ‘assault’ incident
points: LAKSHMI NARAYANAN The AIADMK has announced a protest on November 18, demanding action over an alleged incident in which M.
Ravisankar, the TVK MLA for Thuraiyur and Deputy Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, assaulted a social activist.
In a statement, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K.
Palaniswami alleged that Karthik Kumar, a social activist who went to meet Mr. Ravisankar to submit grievances, was subjected to a “brutal attack” and “verbal abuse”.

Mr. Palaniswami further claimed that after evidence of the assault surfaced, Mr. Ravisankar threatened the activist again and used a police officer to coerce the victim into posting on social media that the incident had never occurred.

Joseph Vijay for remaining silent on the issue, Mr. Palaniswami announced that the AIADMK would stage a condemnation protest at 10 a.m. on Wednesday (November 18 near the Anna Statue at the Thuraiyur bus stand, demanding strict action against Mr. Ravisankar.

items.title: AI Helps Reunite Missing Maharashtra Woman With Family After 2.5 Years
points: A 45-year-old woman who had wandered away from her home in a mentally distressed condition was reunited with her family in Maharashtra's Parbhani district after two-and-a-half years by a social organisation that used AI tools to trace her hometown,…

Julekha Mukheed Shaikh had been admitted to Sanvita Ashram in Pandur, Sindhudurg, on April 3, 2024, following an order from a Metropolitan Magistrate Court in Mumbai's Kurla, issued at the request of the Colaba police and a probation officer at the…
Efforts to locate her family gathered pace after Kisan Choure, trustee of Jeevan Aanand Sanstha, and his team held regular conversations with Shaikh to get clues about her background.
Using digital tools such as Google Search and ChatGPT, the team identified her native place and contacted her relatives with the help of the Nirbhaya police squad in Parbhani, the release said.
Following a phone conversation with her family after two-and-a-half years of separation, her husband, Mukheed Shaikh, travelled to Sanvita Ashram on November 9 and escorted her home.

items.title: 2 Buses Of Punjab Pilgrimage Scheme Collide, 5 Killed In Tarn Taran
points: Five people, including four pilgrims, were killed and more than 15 others injured after two Punjab government-run pilgrimage buses collided head-on on National Highway-54 near Naushehra Pannuan in Tarn Taran district on Saturday evening, officials said.
The buses were carrying pilgrims under the state government's 'Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra Scheme', with 37 people travelling in them.
Tarn Taran Deputy Commissioner Nirmal Ossephchan said four people died on the spot, while one of the six passengers referred to Amritsar succumbed to injuries later.

Five seriously injured passengers were undergoing treatment at Guru Nanak Dev Medical College and Hospital in Amritsar, while the remaining injured were admitted to the Civil Hospital in Tarn Taran, he said.
Earlier, Senior Superintendent of Police Surendra Lamba said a motorcycle pillion rider was among those killed in the accident.
In a post on X, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said he had received distressing news about the accident involving pilgrimage buses near Naushehra Pannuan.

items.title: CM promises govt. support to India’s newest public health university coming up in Hyderabad
points: Revanth Reddy plants a sapling to mark the foundation of PHFI’s campus in Hyderabad on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SIDDHANT THAKUR Chief Minister A.

The Chief Minister recalled how institutions such as the Indian School of Business (ISB) had contributed to Hyderabad’s emergence as an educational and knowledge hub.
Srinath Reddy said PHFI aspired to become the world’s leading public health institution with the establishment of the university in Hyderabad.
Pro-Chancellor Sanjay Zodpey said the university was being conceived as a long-term institution that would serve generations of students, researchers, public health professionals and communities.
He said the public health challenges of the 21st century required professionals with interdisciplinary perspectives, evidence-based knowledge and a commitment to equity and social impact.

He urged participants to develop healthy competition and uphold sportsmanship.

points: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi on Saturday took aim at Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav over his planned visit to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.
He said Muslims had prayed for centuries at the Babri Masjid, which stood on that site until it was demolished in 1992.

"Akhilesh is going to the place where we prayed for 400 years," Owaisi said at a public meeting in Meerut, while also mentioning ASP leader Chandrashekhar Azad's support for people seeking to offer namaz in Nagina.

items.title: After Arnab and Murasu, Andhra Pradesh braces for another cyclonic storm
points: A damaged road at Uppada after Cyclone Arnab made landfall on October 28.
Andhra Pradesh has not seen three consecutive cyclones cross its coast within a month since 1970, says IMD | Photo Credit: File Photo by V.
RAJU After bearing the brunt of Cyclones Arnab and Murasu, Andhra Pradesh is bracing for another cyclonic storm within a week.

According to the latest information from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, the current weather system over the Bay of Bengal may intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 18, and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast.
The current weather models indicate the probability of landfall along the North Coastal Andhra Pradesh on November 19 or 20.

This year, Andhra Pradesh has experienced successive tropical cyclones—very severe cyclonic storm Arnab and severe cyclonic storm Murasu, which made landfall near Narsapur and Ongole, respectively, on the nights of October 28 and November 2.

items.title: VIT-A.P. researchers demonstrate low-cost photonic tech for non-invasive disease screening
points: Scientists from CATS Global (CASTLE Advanced Technologies and Systems), Nashik, Maharashtra, and VIT-A.P.

University, Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, have developed and demonstrated an innovative, low-cost optical sensing approach that could pave the way for affordable, non-invasive disease screening through breath analysis.

According to a press release from the VIT-A.P., the research article titled ‘Photonic elastic-backscatter fingerprinting of exhaled-breath metabolites for non-invasive disease screening’, authored by professors Rao Tatavarti, Sridevi Nadimpalli and P.
Arulmozhivarman Pachiyappan, was published on November 6, 2026, in the international journal Scientific Reports, published by Springer Nature.

The study explores a photonic sensing technique that uses a simple, low-power laser and a position-sensitive optical detector to identify distinctive optical signatures associated with disease-related chemical compounds.
Variations in the concentration of these compounds can be associated with different diseases, making breath analysis a promising approach for non-invasive health screening.

points: A man was seen eating the flesh of a dog killed in a road accident in Odisha's Sambalpur district.
A video of the incident has since gone viral on social media.

points: Keralam Assembly Speaker Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan’s absence from the unveiling of a sculpture honouring endosulfan victims in Kasaragod has triggered a row, with the Speaker and the district panchayat offering conflicting accounts of the happenings.
The Speaker was scheduled to unveil the 40-foot-tall sculpture, titled ‘Victims,’ created by sculptor Kanayi Kunhiraman at the Kasaragod district panchayat office on Friday.
However, he skipped the function and attended another programme in the neighbouring Kannur district.
His absence drew criticism from artists and public representatives, including Manjeswaram MLA A.K.M.

items.title: TVS Motors' 2 Wheeler Business President Quits!
points: TVS Motor Company has announced a senior leadership change in its core Indian two-wheeler business.
Gaurav Gupta, President of the India two-wheeler business, has resigned to pursue an external opportunity and will leave the company at the close of business on December 24, 2026.
From November 20, Aniruddha Haldar will take charge of an expanded role as Senior Vice President, People Mobility, covering the India two-wheeler business.
The company reported 1.9 million vehicle sales in Q2 FY27, its highest-ever quarterly volume, with two-wheeler sales up 27% year-on-year.
Revenue for the quarter rose 44% to Rs 17,103 crore and profit after tax increased 52% to Rs 1,377 crore.
TVS sold 186,186 electric two-wheelers in Q2, up 133% from the same quarter last year.
TVS sold 670,679 two-wheelers during the month, up 28% year-on-year.
Domestic two-wheeler sales rose 22% to 514,764 units, while electric two-wheeler volumes more than doubled to 71,382 units.

items.title: First-Year Student Dies By Suicide At Punjab's Chitkara University Hostel
points: A first-year student at Chitkara University in Punjab has died by suspected suicide, prompting a police investigation.

The girl, identified as Bachelor of Computer Applications (BCA) student Anika Madan, was a resident of Kurukshetra in Haryana and had returned to the university from her home just two days before the incident.
According to university official Sandeep Garg, the incident came to light around 11:30 am when the student's mother, unable to reach her over the phone, alerted the hostel warden.
Following the information, the warden went to the student's room, where the incident was discovered.
No suicide note has been recovered from the room so far, and the circumstances leading to her death remain unclear.

Chitkara University has issued an official statement expressing deep grief over the untimely death of the student.

items.title: 1,000 Drums, 3,000 Dancers: Meghalaya's Wangala Festival Enters Guinness World Records
points: The sound of 1,000 traditional drums filled the Garo Heritage Village in Chibragre, near Tura, as Meghalaya's 100 Drums Wangala Festival entered the Guinness World Records on Saturday.
A total of 1,000 drummers and 3,000 dancers performed together, a milestone in the festival's Golden Jubilee celebrations.
The record-setting performance took place on the last day of the four-day festival, which began on November 11 and ended on November 14.
The 50th edition brought performers and visitors together to celebrate the traditions of the Garo community.
He also conveyed greetings from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the people of the Garo Hills as the festival completed 50 years.
At the festival's inauguration on 11 November, the Chief Minister recalled that his father wanted the 100 Drums Wangala Festival to grow into a much larger event with 1,000 drums.
The 100 Drums Wangala Festival was first held in December 1976 at Asananggre in what was then the West Garo Hills district.
